title: The Monte Carlo Method
claim: Early paper introducing the Monte Carlo method: estimating quantities by random sampling.
venue: Journal of the American Statistical Association

title: On the efficiency of certain quasi-random sequences of points in evaluating multi-dimensional integrals
claim: Introduces the Halton sequence (radical inverses in coprime bases) for multi-dimensional integration.

title: Random Number Generation and Quasi-Monte Carlo Methods
claim: Standard reference for discrepancy, the Koksma–Hlawka inequality and the (log N)^d/N error of QMC.
venue: Society for Industrial and Applied Mathematics

title: Randomization of Number Theoretic Methods for Multiple Integration
claim: Random shift (Cranley–Patterson rotation) of a lattice/point set to get unbiased estimates with error bars.

title: On the convergence rate of randomized quasi-Monte Carlo for discontinuous functions
claim: For discontinuous integrands (like an indicator of a disk) RQMC converges slower than 1/N; rate depends on dimension.
